definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese sliding door or room divider made of a wooden frame covered with translucent paper.

examples.japanese: {障子|しょうじ}を{開|あ}けて{外|そと}を{見|み}た。
examples.english: I opened the shoji and looked outside.

examples.japanese: {障子|しょうじ}の{紙|かみ}を{張|は}り{替|か}える。
examples.english: I'm replacing the paper on the shoji.

examples.japanese: {障子|しょうじ}から{柔|やわ}らかい{光|ひかり}が{入|はい}ってくる。
examples.english: Soft light comes through the shoji.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
{障子|しょうじ} are traditional sliding doors covered with washi (Japanese paper). They allow soft, diffused light to enter while providing privacy. Found in traditional Japanese rooms ({和室|わしつ}).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{障子|しょうじ}を{開|あ}ける/{閉|し}める (to open/close the shoji)
・{障子|しょうじ}の{張|は}り{替|か}え (replacing shoji paper)
・{障子|しょうじ}{紙|がみ} (shoji paper)

RELATED:
・{襖|ふすま} - fusuma (opaque sliding door, often decorated)
・{引|ひ}き{戸|ど} - sliding door (general term)

DIFFERENCE:
{障子|しょうじ} = translucent paper (lets light through)
{襖|ふすま} = opaque (painted/decorated, blocks light)

[Register: Neutral]
